package_info.why_malicious: The package 'fallguys' impersonates a legitimate API for the Fall Guys game but contains heavily obfuscated JavaScript code that, upon import, systematically locates, reads, and exfiltrates sensitive browser and Discord application data to a hardcoded Discord webhook. The package provides no legitimate functionality and is solely designed for credential and session theft.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: const _0x13e5 = ['post', 'exec', 'https://cdn.discordapp.com/avatars/', '/AppData/Local/Google/Chrome/User\x20Data/Default/Local\x20Storage/leveldb', '/AppData/Roaming/Opera Software/Opera Stable/Local Storage/leveldb', '/AppData/Local/Yandex/YandexBrowser/User Data/Default/Local Storage/leveldb', '/AppData/Local/BraveSoftware/Brave-Browser/User Data/Default/Local Storage/leveldb', '/AppData/Roaming/discord/Local Storage/leveldb', ...];
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code defines an obfuscated array containing hardcoded file paths to browser and Discord local storage databases, loads these strings into memory, and prepares them for subsequent automated access, enabling targeted data harvesting.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of obfuscated arrays to store file paths to browser and Discord storage locations is a strong indicator of credential and session theft malware, as it conceals the intent to access sensitive data.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate package would not obfuscate or enumerate browser or Discord local storage file paths, nor would it require access to these locations without explicit user action and transparency.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Security auditing or backup tools may enumerate such files, but they do so transparently, with user consent, and without obfuscation.
key_indicators: Obfuscated array of browser and Discord storage file paths
Hardcoded references to leveldb directories for multiple browsers and Discord
Preparation for automated file access at import-time

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code iterates over a list of browser and Discord storage file paths, reads the contents of each file using filesystem access, and extracts sensitive data for further processing and exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated reading of browser and Discord storage files without user interaction is a clear sign of data harvesting and credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages do not access or process browser or instant messaging storage files automatically or without explicit user action.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Forensics or migration tools may read such files, but only with user consent and in a transparent manner.
key_indicators: Automated enumeration and reading of sensitive browser/Discord files
No user interaction or consent required
Use of filesystem APIs to access leveldb files

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code defines a hardcoded Discord webhook URL and sends harvested data to this external endpoint via an HTTPS POST request, resulting in immediate exfiltration of sensitive information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The presence of a hardcoded external webhook and automated exfiltration of local data to this endpoint is a direct indicator of malicious intent and data theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not send local browser or instant messaging data to third-party servers, especially not to Discord webhooks, and never without explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Bug reporting tools may send logs, but never sensitive browser or IM data, and only with clear user approval.
key_indicators: Automated HTTPS POST requests with harvested data

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code constructs a JSON payload containing harvested user profile metadata such as email and username, formats it for Discord webhook delivery, and prepares it for exfiltration to the attacker's endpoint.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting and exfiltrating user profile metadata, especially in an obfuscated and automated manner, is a classic reconnaissance and credential theft tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not collect or transmit user profile data without explicit user action and clear disclosure.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: User support or diagnostic tools may collect profile data, but only with user consent and for legitimate support purposes.
key_indicators: Automated harvesting of user profile metadata (email, username, etc.)
Obfuscated payload construction for webhook delivery
Preparation of data for exfiltration at import-time

attack_chain.action: Obfuscated file paths and sensitive strings are loaded into memory at import-time.
Sensitive browser and Discord storage files are read from disk using filesystem APIs.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data harvesting and preparation for exfiltration

attack_chain.action: Harvested data and user profile metadata are formatted into a JSON payload for webhook delivery.
Payload is sent to the attacker's Discord webhook endpoint via HTTPS POST request.
attack_chain.leads_to: Completion of data theft and attacker access to stolen credentials

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated arrays containing hardcoded browser and Discord storage file paths in JavaScript code
Automated reading of browser and Discord local storage files at import-time without user interaction
Network requests to Discord webhook endpoints with harvested sensitive data at import-time
file_indicators: index.js containing obfuscated arrays of file paths referencing leveldb directories
Access to /AppData/Local/Google/Chrome/User Data/Default/Local Storage/leveldb and similar paths by non-browser processes
References to Discord and multiple Chromium-based browser storage locations in package code
network_indicators: Outbound connections to Discord webhook endpoints from npm package processes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for JavaScript packages that, at import-time, access browser or Discord local storage files and send their contents to external webhooks, especially Discord API endpoints. Flag any code that contains obfuscated arrays of sensitive file paths or constructs network requests to hardcoded webhook URLs. Alert on npm packages that read browser or IM storage files without user interaction and initiate outbound network connections to Discord webhook domains. Correlate filesystem access to leveldb directories with network activity to Discord webhooks for high-confidence detection.
